statements.summary: Project brief details for Campus Room Booking prepared by Northfield College Facilities Office.

citations.quote: # Campus Room Booking: Project Brief
Prepared by the Facilities Office, Northfield College. Synthetic example; all names are fictional. Date: 2 September 2026.
## Background

statements.summary: Current library room booking process uses email requests and a spreadsheet, causing frequent double bookings.

citations.quote: Students and staff book the 24 group-study rooms in the library by emailing the Facilities Office. Requests are tracked in a shared spreadsheet, double bookings happen several times a week, and nobody can see which rooms are free without asking.

statements.summary: Project goals include letting users see free rooms and book themselves, eliminating double bookings, and providing a single booking view for Facilities.

citations.quote: ## Goals

- Let students and staff see which study rooms are free and book one themselves.
- Reduce double bookings to zero.
- Give the Facilities Office a single view of all bookings.

statements.summary: First release scope covers existing college account sign-in, searching by date/time/capacity, one-off slot booking, a 4-hour limit, and room blocking for maintenance.

citations.quote: ## In scope for the first release

- Students and staff sign in with their existing college account.
- A user can search rooms by date, time and capacity, and book an individual one-off slot.
- A booking can last up to 4 hours.
- The Facilities Office can block a room for maintenance.

statements.summary: No-shows and cancellation policies remain open pending discussion between Facilities and Student Services.

citations.quote: ## Open points
We have not yet agreed what happens when someone cannot attend a booking. The Facilities Office will discuss this with Student Services.

statements.summary: Kickoff meeting attendee list includes project sponsor, student representative, IT developer, and product owner.

citations.quote: # Kickoff meeting: Campus Room Booking

Attendees: Dana Ruiz (Facilities Manager, project sponsor), Sam Okafor (Student Union representative), Priya Nair (IT developer), Alex Kim (product owner). Synthetic transcript; all names are fictional.
**Alex (Product owner):** Thanks for coming. Today we agree what goes into the first release of room booking.

statements.summary: The booking service will reject overlapping bookings for the same room to eliminate double bookings.

citations.quote: The main thing for us is ending double bookings. If two people can take the same room at the same time, we have failed.
The booking service will reject an overlapping booking for the same room. That part is straightforward.

statements.summary: Students mostly want rooms for single study sessions before exams.

citations.quote: Students mostly want a room for a single study session, usually a couple of hours before an exam.

statements.summary: Student Union proposed recurring bookings for societies every Tuesday evening.

citations.quote: Could societies book the same room every week, say every Tuesday evening?

statements.summary: Recurring bookings are excluded from the first release.

citations.quote: Not in the first release. Recurring bookings make the clash rules much harder, so let's leave recurring bookings out for now and revisit after launch.
Recurring reservations are out of scope for release one.

statements.summary: The maximum duration for a single booking is reduced from four hours to three hours.

citations.quote: The brief says four hours, but three hours is the most I want for a single booking, or rooms get hogged.

statements.summary: IT proposed syncing bookings to people's Outlook calendars.

citations.quote: Maybe we could also sync bookings to people's Outlook calendars? It might be nice.
Possibly, but let's not commit to that today.

statements.summary: Cancellation rules and no-show handling remain open until Dana confirms with Student Services.

citations.quote: What happens if a student books a room and doesn't turn up? Some rooms sit empty all afternoon.
We need a rule for no-shows, and for how late someone can cancel, but I have to check with Student Services first.
Okay, cancellation and no-shows stay open until Dana confirms.

statements.summary: The Facilities Office needs to see who booked each room, but students should only see that a room is taken without identifying the booker.

citations.quote: Also, my office needs to see who booked each room. Students should only see that a room is taken, not who took it.
Good. Let's wrap up there.

items.title: Room Booking and Availability Management
items.description: Enables users to search and book study rooms while preventing clashes and managing capacity.

items.title: Administration and Access Control
items.description: Provides facilities staff with administrative views, college account sign-in, and maintenance blocking.

items.title: Sign in with college account
items.description: As a student or staff member, I want to sign in with my existing college account, so that I can access the booking system.

criteria.text: When a user attempts to sign in with valid college credentials, authentication succeeds and the user is granted access.

items.title: Search and book rooms
items.description: As a user, I want to search rooms by date, time and capacity, and book an individual one-off slot, so that I can secure a study space.

criteria.text: When a user searches by date, time, and capacity, matching available rooms are displayed.

citations.quote: A user can search rooms by date, time and capacity, and book an individual one-off slot.

items.title: Enforce booking duration limit
items.description: As a user, I want a booking to last up to 3 hours, so that rooms do not get hogged.

criteria.text: When a user attempts to book a single slot exceeding 3 hours, the booking is rejected.

citations.quote: three hours is the most I want for a single booking, or rooms get hogged.

items.title: Reject overlapping bookings
items.description: As a project stakeholder, I want the booking service to reject an overlapping booking for the same room, so that double bookings are eliminated.

criteria.text: When a user tries to book a room for a time slot that overlaps with an existing reservation, the booking service rejects the overlapping booking.

citations.quote: The booking service will reject an overlapping booking for the same room.

items.title: Block a room for maintenance
items.description: As a Facilities Office staff member, I want to block a room for maintenance, so that users cannot book unavailable rooms.

criteria.text: When facilities staff block a room for maintenance, the room becomes unbookable for that period.

citations.quote: The Facilities Office can block a room for maintenance.

items.title: Facilities Office single booking view
items.description: As a Facilities Office staff member, I want to see who booked each room, so that my office has a single view of all bookings.

criteria.text: When facilities staff view room bookings, the system displays the identity of the user who booked each room.

citations.quote: my office needs to see who booked each room.

items.title: Student view of room availability
items.description: As a student, I want to see that a room is taken without seeing who took it, so that privacy is maintained.

criteria.text: When a student views a booked room, the system indicates that the room is taken without revealing the booker's identity.

citations.quote: Students should only see that a room is taken, not who took it.

questions.subject: Cancellation and no-show policies
questions.question: What are the specific rules and penalties for no-shows and how late someone can cancel a booking?
questions.why_it_matters: It is currently undecided and requires confirmation from Student Services before implementation.

citations.quote: We have not yet agreed what happens when someone cannot attend a booking. The Facilities Office will discuss this with Student Services.
We need a rule for no-shows, and for how late someone can cancel, but I have to check with Student Services first.
